sections.html: San Angelo is the Tom Green County seat, built where three Concho rivers meet. Buyers here come from Goodfellow Air Force Base, Angelo State University, the hospitals and the ranching trade, so demand shifts with those employers. The older blocks near downtown and Fort Concho have their own following. The 2000 population was 88,439.

In San Angelo you can hire an agent, go it alone as a for-sale-by-owner, or hand the keys to an investor who buys as-is. Which one fits depends mostly on your calendar.

An agent listing shows the house to the widest pool, and it rewards a sound roof, working systems and fresh cosmetics. Expect buyer loans, an appraisal and a round of repair haggling along the way. An investor offer trims nearly all of that and closes whenever you pick. The trade is a price that sits under what a polished listing might fetch.

  • Get each buyer's closing timeline and ask who covers title and recording fees.
  • Hold a written bid in hand before you pull the listing.
  • File every contract and repair credit where you can find it.

The Tom Green County Appraisal District runs the parcel search. Open your account, click the Tax Summary tab, and you will see the balance plus a link to pay by electronic check or card.

For 2026 the district named midnight on May 15 as the protest deadline for many residential parcels and told owners to match it against the notice they received. You could email a protest, mail it with a postmark, drop it in the box or file it online. Business personal property owners send rendition forms to a separate email address. Print the tax summary before you list, so you and the buyer work from the same figures.

The year runs from the January valuation to the January payment cutoff.

Property tax dates for Tom Green County owners
DateWhat happens
January 2 to April 15Rendition period for most property types
April 1Notices for single-family homesteads mailed, or soon after
July 25Appraisal roll certified to taxing units
October 1Tax bills mailed
November 30First half due under the split option
June 30Second half due under the split option

Spring listers should watch for homestead notices around April 1 and other property notices near May 1. A changed value can show up mid-sale, so warn your buyer ahead of time. The Comptroller deadlines page has the full list.

February 1 is the day a still-open bill becomes delinquent. Because the lien rides along with the house, somebody has to pay it or set up a plan before the deed can change hands.

The collector tacks on a 6 percent penalty plus 1 percent interest, and interest then grows by another percent every month. In July the penalty climbs to 12 percent, and interest has no ceiling. If the taxing unit brings in its lawyer, collection costs of up to 20 percent can be stacked onto the balance. If you pay within three weeks of learning the bill was late, a written waiver request may help in some cases. Years of neglect can bring a lawsuit and a tax sale, and the former owner then has two years to claim any money left over.

  • Find out if a partial payment gets credited against the oldest year before the newer ones.
  • Homestead owners may ask for an installment plan stretching up to 36 months.
  • Order a tax certificate well ahead of closing. The title company settles old tax from your proceeds at closing.

Start with the homestead exemption, then check the extra layers for older owners, disabled owners and service-connected disability.

Every school district has to leave $140,000 of a homestead's value untaxed, and owners who are seniors or disabled get $60,000 more. Counties that charge farm-to-market or flood control taxes subtract $3,000. Older and disabled owners also get a frozen school tax amount, and the freeze can follow them, in proportion, to a later Texas homestead. If you sell mid-year to a buyer who lives there and you had no exemption, the buyer may claim it for whatever remains of that year. An owner with a service disability can take $5,000 to $12,000 off the value, and a 100 percent rating means the whole homestead is exempt.

Renters do not have to leave because you sold. A buyer who wants the place empty, though, depends on the landlord winning a Texas eviction first.

With no lease clause on the point, the landlord first hands over a written notice giving three days, then sues in justice court. A hearing date falls 10 to 21 days after filing, and the tenant gets served four days before it. Appealing to county court is allowed, within five days of the judgment. A writ cannot issue until six days after judgment, and the constable posts 24 hours' notice before carrying it out. Buyers who accept the tenant in place never face this process.

Learn whether the previous owner left a will. The answer tells you which court document the buyer's closer will want to see.

Texas gives heirs until four years after the death to offer a will for probate, normally in the home county. If the only debts are liens on the real estate, a muniment of title can move the house to the heirs, with the court order and will filed in the county where the land sits. For estates with no will and no administration, a small estate affidavit works if the value outside the homestead is no more than $75,000. An heirship affidavit is just a sworn statement, and outsiders such as a title company can turn it down.

  • Pull together the death certificate and whatever deed is recorded.
  • Ask the appraisal district what heirs must file to keep a homestead exemption.
  • Talk to a probate lawyer before you sign a purchase contract.

Texas power-of-sale foreclosure follows a set schedule. Selling ahead of it is how owners hold on to whatever equity they have.

Once the lender sends its default notice, you have 20 days to pay the arrears and reinstate. Then comes a sale notice, posted at least three weeks before an auction on the first Tuesday of a month, at a spot the commissioners court has designated. Any surplus after the lender is paid reaches junior lienholders first, with the remainder yours. If the sale falls short, the lender can chase the difference for two years. A cash buyer able to close inside that window may be your only way to sell in time.

sections.h2: What changes with a cash buyer
sections.html: A cash deal removes the buyer's mortgage, the appraisal and most repair credits. You still need clean title, a signed contract and an agreed closing day. Take your photo ID, the deed or inheritance papers and your latest tax summary to the title company. Settle who pays title and recording fees before you sign, and review the closing statement a day ahead so nothing catches you off guard.

faqs.q: What county is San Angelo in?
faqs.a: Tom Green County. San Angelo is the county seat, and the appraisal district there keeps the property records.

faqs.q: Can I pay San Angelo property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes. The district's Tax Summary page has a pay link for electronic check or card. Confirm current options with the tax office.

faqs.q: Must I clear old taxes before selling?
faqs.a: Closing proceeds cover any old tax, since the lien stays with the house. Get a tax certificate from the title company beforehand.

faqs.q: When does a protest hearing happen?
faqs.a: Hearings begin around mid May, and the review board approves the roll by July 20. Miss the filing deadline and you lose the hearing.

faqs.q: What does a cash buyer pay for in San Angelo?
faqs.a: It varies by buyer. Get the bid in writing and see who covers title, recording and repairs before you sign.
